text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish banks losing tens of billions of markka in performing credit as companies increasingly pay off old loans by obtaining foreign financing at lower rates.

- Government to make two top applicants compete for nationwide commercial TV channel -- wants to see which is ready to do most to develop terrestrial digital network. Decision on licence award expected next week. @
- Complaint lodged with Equality Ombudsman after Helsinki's all-male stock exchange club refused to serve dinner to woman guest.
- Government approved plan to raise Finland's development aid to 0.4 percent of GDP by the year 2000 from current level of just over 0.3 percent.
- New Finnish corporate law unlikely to take effect before end-year, small businesses oppose increase in minimum share capital requirement to 50,000 markka. @

- Cooperation between Finnish industry and academic research institutions is excellent, says Nokia research chief Yrjo Neuvo, reacting to allegations that Finnish firms' inadequate research support benefits foreign competitors.
- Harvard Management Company has bought large stake in Sampo, becoming fifth largest owner.

- European Commissioner Erkki Liikanen said enlargement of EU into central and east Europe would probably take place in two waves. He said expansion would depend on a fundamental reform of of EU administration and agricultural support. @
- Second Social and Health Minister Terttu Huttu-Junttunen ready to try distributing syringes to drug users in an effort to cut risks of HIV infection. Proposal has numerous opponents.

- The further to the east the EU can expand, the safer Europe will be, said European MP Otto von Habsburg on a visit to Turku. Von Habsburg said Europe should give a clear signal that the Baltic states will not be left as a target for Russia.
- Finland will continue to pay subsidies to shipyards as long as other EU countries continue to do so, Minister of Trade and Industry Antti Kalliomaki said. @
